Why does a cold can sweat?
Why does a cold can sweat?
The water isn't leaking
out.
The can is sealed.
Warm air is full of
invisible water vapour.
On a hot,
humid day,
one cubic metre of air
carries about 25 grams of it.
The air touching a can
from the fridge chills
to nearly fridge
temperature.
That cold,
no more than about six
grams per cubic metre
can stay as vapour.
The rest has nowhere to
go,
so it turns back into
liquid,
right on the can.
It's the same as morning
dew,
or the fog on your
glasses when you step
out of an
air-conditioned room.
The can isn't sweating.
The air is.
